extracted.intended_audience: editors, newsroom managers and journalists reporting on elections
extracted.subtask_description: Operational and ethical guidance for editors and reporters organising newsroom election coverage, including planning, social media verification, public engagement, safety, budgeting and editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan early and seriously
rubrics_metrics.description: Elections are a mix of rules and chaos; make sure to plan early and seriously enough to handle predictable events and surprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for the 24-hour cycle, resource needs, likely scenarios and contingencies so the newsroom can address the campaign's rollercoaster and ups and downs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek guarantees for journalist safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek guarantees from government and political parties about safety and security of journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with other media or unions to draft charters committing parties to respect and protect journalists; set up monitoring and rapid response for aggression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject manipulation and paid-for journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid all attempts to manipulate media or use corrupt processes, such as paid-for journalism, to distort coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be vigilant for attempts by political actors to buy or distort coverage and have editorial rules that forbid such practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish common standards and eliminate hate speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish common standards of reporting that will confront and eliminate all forms of political speech that is hateful or inciting violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agree newsroom-wide standards and moderation policies to identify and remove inciting or hateful political speech across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election coverage training with ethical core
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide election coverage training that puts ethical standards at the heart of any course and uses best training modules and approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train reporters and editors on hate-speech dangers, sectarianism and extremism; involve editors; organise training in advance and during the election period as part of a strategic programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote free media and protect journalistic independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments must avoid imposing forms of regulation that may curb independence of journalism and must protect rights of media and citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate transparent, professional and independent media accountability; promote access to public information and ICT to enable citizen participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core journalistic principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should 'tell the truth', 'be independent', 'strive for impartiality', 'minimise harm', and 'be accountable'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these principles as the underpinning ethical framework for all election reporting and editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint social media editors and teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor the social media universe by appointing a social media editor and a team of social media reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign staff to monitor websites, Twitter, Facebook and other feeds for early warning, fact-checking, rumours, quotes, profiles and mood indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train reporters in data mining and verification for social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters must be trained in data mining and in verification techniques specifically tailored to social media’s frenzied tempo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide instruction on tracing sources, verifying images and videos, and evaluating automated/social data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow candidates' social media and analyse discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow candidates’ own social media as they increasingly use Twitter or Facebook as campaigning tools; analyse their discourse and compare with rivals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check popularity metrics but treat them cautiously; use social feeds for quotes, alerts and connections, not as definitive evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish regular social media updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish regular updates on the social media scene highlighting trends and notable activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include what’s trending, tallies of followers/friends, likes on issues, network connections that reveal affiliations, and analysis of popular retweets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorously verify social media content
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat social media as a source but verify comments and claims independently and rigorously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat social media as scientific polling; fact-check rumours and avoid trusting social-media-based predictions of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use website as one-stop electoral information hub
rubrics_metrics.description: Your website should inform, educate and sometimes entertain; provide practical citizen-oriented information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include electoral calendars, voter procedures, candidates' verbatim statements, background materials and reference documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide continuous online reporting and user-generated content
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer permanent updates and reporting online, incorporating journalists' own tweets and vetted user-generated content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate traditional and online operations so the site can offer the full gamut of journalistic forms and values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open space for opinions and guest debate with standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the web to host opinions and debates, inviting guest columnists and public interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept citizen bloggers based on talent, adherence to journalistic standards, and original perspective; be transparent about op-ed policies and distinguish independent commentary from partisan advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use entertaining formats carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Lighten up coverage using games and interactive formats to educate, but avoid trivialising the election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect strict criteria for online surveys (confidentiality, design) and avoid turning coverage into pure infotainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stenography and 'he said/she said' reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not let journalists become megaphones or stenographers of political candidates' talk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act as an umpire and steward of the electoral race—analyse claims, provide context and avoid simple point-counterpoint reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask 'what's missing' and be inclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: Constantly ask what is missing in current coverage and whether coverage has been inclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report on neglected issues and social groups, give voice to smaller parties and local concerns, and avoid concentrating only on star politicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat and explain complex basics as needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't assume audiences have prior knowledge—repeat the basics of difficult issues when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid newsroom cynicism ('we've already done it') and ensure stories remain accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify and demystify jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Make stories and issues accessible by decoding political jargon, abbreviations and acronyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track down and eliminate long words or acronyms that make concepts incomprehensible to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pack journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware of pack behaviour that leads multiple outlets to cover the same events and interpret them identically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert when a candidate rises in polls or a controversy breaks and avoid replicating uniform narratives without independent verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose political spin and scrutinise campaign techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyse campaign strategies, political advertising, stunts and tricks; scrutinise promises and press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissect advertising techniques, check for approximation, falsification and distortion, and call out spin publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track promises and inconsistencies over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember and check what candidates said and did over years, not just days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records and follow-up stories that test pledges against actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the money
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate who finances campaigns, the interests behind funding and potential conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask who benefits from proposed policies and whether donors influence outcomes; examine campaign finance and regulatory implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess newsworthiness; avoid overhyping controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not treat every outrageous statement as inherently newsworthy; evaluate context and source importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid amplifying contrived rumour campaigns that distract from voters' real interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise caution on election night returns
rubrics_metrics.description: When votes are counted, do not rush to judgement on early returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with initial results; verify processes and avoid premature declarations that may be embarrassing later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow every link back to original sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Always trace online links back to the original material and evaluate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following chains of links improves accuracy and can reveal more important or differently emphasised original reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't retweet or share without checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not retweet links you haven’t clicked or share content you haven’t examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click through to original content, check context, and avoid amplifying mistaken or partial accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch videos yourself rather than relying on others' summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Never use quotes or descriptions of a video from another story without watching the video yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original video may include omitted material; confirm context and content directly before reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify social media account credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider a tweeter's identity and past behaviour before trusting their material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Google handles, check bios and past tweets, test location consistency, and compare with official agency tweets for confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify potential fake accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use practical checks to spot fake or anonymous accounts when covering elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for missing real names in bios, conflicting locations, try DM/@ enquiries, and be sceptical of non-journalists using journalistic language or claiming 'BREAKING NEWS'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misinterpreting social media sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not draw broad conclusions about public mood from social network posts alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember not everyone uses social media and metrics are not representative of the wider electorate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualify and pace reporting when information is unconfirmed
rubrics_metrics.description: When hearing reports of winners or breaking claims, ask origin and verification before asserting facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate status to the audience (e.g., 'X is reporting Y, but we haven't yet confirmed') and provide updates as verification progresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct social media errors proactively and visibly
rubrics_metrics.description: If misinformation was spread online, take steps to correct it widely and repeatedly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tweet corrections multiple times, identify influential spreaders of the error and ask for help distributing the correction; correct across all platforms where the falsehood circulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check with electoral authorities and study election rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the electoral commission on registration dates, campaign periods, election-day logistics and timetables for returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study voting systems, electoral laws, poll reporting rules, political advertising rules, access to public media, electoral expenses, and observer rules to inform coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure newsroom understands and can verify rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure all journalists understand election rules and are trained to verify violations independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain rules to readers, provide reporting guidelines, and enable staff to spot and document breaches without partisan reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve non-political desks in coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Election coverage should not be exclusive to the political desk; other departments should contribute according to their beats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign specialised reporters (economics, health, labour, education, sports) to analyse party programmes, scrutinise speeches, and investigate international or diaspora angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan election-night logistics and coverage formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Organise a fool-proof election-night reporting system covering major party HQs, expert commentary and communications needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange advance appointments for comments, design attractive yet substantive formats, check transport, phones and Wi‑Fi, and ensure technical redundancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use experts and pundits judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Have analysts and commentators on standby but avoid overwhelming audiences with excessive punditry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance expert analysis with ordinary citizens’ voices to give breadth and grounding to coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruit additional personnel for election period
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring in extra staff (young journalists, phone operators, secretaries, drivers) to handle information flow on election day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan human resources ahead to manage higher workloads and real-time reporting demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan technical and operational arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate with production managers to provide extra airtime/pages and later deadlines; beef up reporting teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide ad-free programming or pages, set guidelines for political advertising placement, and ensure production capacity for extended coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan emergency procedures for technical failures, inaccessible journalists, injured or arrested reporters, or political meltdowns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have redundancies for systems, communication plans and protocols to continue reporting under duress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precook predictable outputs and prepare resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare candidate profiles, district close-ups and the reporting format you will use to report results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile background files (photos, video, sound), demographic and economic data for districts, and pre-drafted pieces to speed accurate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget for election reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate resources for extra phone lines, routers, transmission capacity, vehicles, overtime and other costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan budgets carefully, consider partnerships with non-rival media to share costs for polls, investigations or pundits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold ethics: facts over opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Election reporting tests media ethics: when opinion is free, facts are sacred; practise honesty, fairness and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject manipulation and incitement to hatred; be responsible for keeping the electoral process open, peaceful, free and fair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign a public editor or ombudsman
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign someone to hear public reactions and complaints and relay them to editorial staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the public editor to correct and improve election reporting and to maintain accountability to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest in staff roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Double-check staff party membership, donations or potentially compromising activities that could bias coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent staff participation in party events, paid training for candidates, or other activities that undermine editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisit and restate the editorial line before campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss and clarify your editorial line well before the election to avoid fuzzy, contradictory or simplistic commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate difficult questions and remind staff of core values; keep news sections separate from editorials and maintain journalists' freedom to pursue truth and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define op-ed policy and page rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide who is allowed or banned from op-ed spaces and be transparent about criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be pluralistic but clear; explain norms to the public; make a visual distinction between independent commentary and partisan advocacy; consider temporary columnists during campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public opinion polls responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat opinion polls as useful but potentially distorting: avoid turning campaigns into horse races dominated by poll positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain methodological conditions and limits when publishing polls, expose fraud, and ensure polls do not replace traditional reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Go out and report on the ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritise traditional on-the-street deep reporting to take the pulse of the electorate and identify issues polls miss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send reporters to diverse areas, conduct deep interviews rather than superficial vox pops, and contextualise citizens' comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vox pops carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Short street interviews are popular but can mislead if presented as representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mock interviewees, choose them for news and opinion value, and avoid using vox pops as marketing or artificial representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderate public forums and enforce anti-hate rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Define moderation rules for online forums, chats, live exchanges; confront and eliminate hate speech and prevent hijacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set and announce policies on anonymity and acceptable behaviour; guard public spaces against incendiary or ad hominem attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve the public in newsgathering with verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit public contributions for election news and appoint a public reporters' editor to vet incoming material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interns or staff to double-check and validate crowdsourced information before using it in coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner with NGOs and citizen monitoring projects carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with specialised NGOs or citizen-journalist platforms for monitoring and information but maintain editorial control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner to gain coverage breadth (e.g., human-rights monitors, Ushahidi-like projects) but avoid becoming an advocate for an advocacy organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct risk assessments and safety training for staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Make risk assessments and security arrangements early; train journalists and set emergency procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider coordinated action with media unions, draft protection charters, and set up independent monitoring groups to investigate aggression toward the press.
